subject: Samples
title: Demo Pack
notes: Generic sample questions demonstrating all five question types.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits at an average distance of about 58 million kilometers from the Sun, making it the closest planet. Venus, Earth, and Mars orbit progressively farther out, so each is more distant than Mercury.

questions.prompt: At standard atmospheric pressure, at what temperature does pure water boil?
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere, or 101.325 kilopascals), pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit). 90 degrees Celsius is wrong because water reaches that temperature without a phase change at standard pressure; it is the boiling point only at reduced pressure, such as at high altitude. 110 degrees Celsius is wrong because water reaches it only under pressure above 1 atmosphere, as in a pressure cooker. 0 degrees Celsius is wrong because that is the freezing point, the solid-liquid transition rather than the liquid-gas one.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly pair an SI unit with the quantity it measures? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Kelvin is the International System of Units (SI) base unit of thermodynamic temperature and Pascal is the SI derived unit of pressure, so both pairings are correct. 'Ampere measures frequency' is wrong because the Ampere is the base unit of electric current; frequency is measured in Hertz. 'Hertz measures electric current' is wrong for the same reason reversed: Hertz is the derived unit of frequency, one cycle per second. The two incorrect options swap the quantities measured by Ampere and Hertz.

questions.prompt: A library charges $0.25 per day for overdue books. You borrowed a book on March 1 and returned it on March 15. The loan period is 7 days. How much do you owe in late fees?
questions.explanation: The book was due on March 8 (7 days after March 1). It was returned on March 15, which is 7 days overdue. 7 days multiplied by $0.25 per day equals $1.75 in late fees.

questions.prompt: In what year did the first Moon landing occur?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, when Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the lunar surface. The other options are nearby years offered as plausible distractors, but the first crewed landing was specifically 1969 — not 1965, 1967, or 1971.

questions.prompt: Which of the following bodies are planets in our solar system? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Mars and Jupiter are planets that orbit the Sun directly. Europa and Titan are not planets: Europa is a moon of Jupiter and Titan is a moon of Saturn, so each orbits a planet rather than the Sun.
